summary: Registers the URN Namespace Identifier "nena" for resources published by the National Emergency Number Association, whose resources are managed through the NENA Registry System. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This reserves a name prefix so an emergency-number organization can give permanent names to its documents and resources.

questions: urn namespace for emergency number association
subtitle: Reserve the URN prefix 'nena' for the emergency services organization to identify resources.

tldr.problem: The National Emergency Number Association needs to create and identify resources for IP-based emergency services networks, and requires a unique, persistent namespace so that resources can be referenced reliably.
tldr.mechanism: Register a Uniform Resource Name (URN) Namespace Identifier 'nena' with IANA and define the structure for URNs under that namespace. NENA's Registry System (NRS) manages the namespace.
tldr.outcome: NENA can now assign stable, unique identifiers to its resources like service descriptions and capabilities, enabling IP-based emergency services (ESInet) standards. This is an Informational RFC.

today: RFC 6061 is an Informational RFC published in January 2011. It established the urn:nena namespace for NENA resources, and the namespace remains in active use by NENA for emergency services standards and specifications.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The National Emergency Number Association (NENA) is developing IP-based emergency services networks (ESInet) for public safety in North America. To build these networks, NENA creates standards and technical specifications that define various resources and services. Some of these resources, especially XML namespaces and data models, need unique and persistent identifiers that will not conflict with other organizations' identifiers.

RFC 6061 registers the URN Namespace Identifier (NID) nena with IANA. This allows NENA to create Uniform Resource Names (URNs) starting with urn:nena: to identify its resources. The namespace is managed by NENA's Registry System (NRS), which maintains the official registry of all NENA-defined resources and services.
sections.plainLanguage: Emergency services organizations need permanent names for their standards and documents. This document reserves a name prefix just for them.

sections.title: The NENA URN Namespace
sections.content:
The registered Namespace Identifier is nena. URNs in this namespace follow the structure urn:nena:{NENAclass}:{ClassSpecificString}.

The first part after the colon, the NENAclass, is a high-level category. Examples might be service types or resource types. Each NENAclass has its own specific labeling and registry rules, defined in NENA standards documents. New top-level NENAclass entries require publication of a full NENA Technical Standard document.

The second part, the ClassSpecificString, is specific to each class. For example, within the emergencyresponders class, URNs like urn:nena:emergencyresponders:ambulance, urn:nena:emergencyresponders:fire, and urn:nena:emergencyresponders:police identify different types of responders.
sections.plainLanguage: Names are like a filing system: a broad category, then a specific item in that category.

sections.title: Management and Registration
sections.content:
NENA's Registry System (NRS) owns and manages the entire urn:nena namespace. The NRS is responsible for ensuring uniqueness of all registered URNs and maintaining clear documentation of each resource.

Subregistries for specific NENAclasses can be established by NENA technical standards. These subregistries may have different management policies (such as 'expert review' or 'first come, first served') as defined in NENA standard 70-001, but the NRS retains overall control and will not delegate management to external organizations.

The NRS maintains a public website at a stable URL that displays both HTML and XML versions of the namespace registry, allowing vendors and other organizations to discover NENA-defined resources. When 3GPP or other standards bodies want to reference a NENA resource, they can look it up in the public registry.
sections.plainLanguage: One organization, NENA, keeps the master list of all names in their namespace. They have rules for how new names are added.

sections.title: Scope and Use
sections.content:
The scope of the urn:nena namespace is global. NENA resources may be referenced by any organization or system that interacts with NENA standards. Resources defined by NENA that use this namespace are generally available for use by other organizations within the constraints of NENA's defined processes.

The primary motivation for this namespace is to support NENA's work on IP-based Emergency Services IP Networks (ESInet). Many of the solutions developed by NENA require XML namespaces and identifiers that are unique, persistent, and resolvable. Examples include service descriptions, capability definitions, and protocol parameters used in emergency communications systems.

Unlike some URN namespaces that may be used only within a single closed environment, the urn:nena namespace is designed for both internal NENA use and for reference by external systems that need to interoperate with NENA-based emergency services.
sections.plainLanguage: Emergency services can be in any country, so these names need to work globally. Hospitals, police, and fire departments all over need to use these standard names.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R., and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
